statement.en: This level is set in the foothills of south-western Alberta, where the plains meet the Rocky Mountains. These are the lands of Treaty No. 7, made on 22 September 1877. The treaty marks out its own boundary. The land starts at the United States border and runs north. Its western edge is “the central range of the Rocky Mountains”, and the treaty lands sit east of that range. The treaty places them “south and west of Treaties numbers six and four”. Its seven First Nations are the Bearspaw, the Chiniki, the Wesley, the Blood Tribe, the Piikani Nation, the Siksika Nation and the Tsuut'ina Nation.
statement.fr: Ce niveau se déroule dans les contreforts du sud-ouest de l'Alberta, là où les plaines rencontrent les Rocheuses. Ces terres sont visées par le Traité no 7, conclu le 22 septembre 1877. Le traité trace lui-même sa frontière. Le territoire part de la frontière des États-Unis et s'étend vers le nord. Sa limite ouest est « la chaîne centrale des montagnes Rocheuses », et les terres du traité se trouvent à l'est de cette chaîne. Le traité les situe « au sud et à l'ouest des Traités numéros six et quatre ». Ses sept Premières Nations sont les Bearspaw, les Chiniki, les Wesley, la Tribu des Blood, la Nation Piikani, la Nation Siksika et la Nation Tsuut'ina.

source.quote: the Territory north of the United States Boundary Line, east of the central range of the Rocky Mountains, and south and west of Treaties numbers six and four

verification.evidence: the Treaty made and concluded at the Blackfoot Crossing of the Bow River, on the twenty-second day of September, in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and seventy-seven … all their rights, titles, and privileges whatsoever to the lands included within the following limits, that is to say: Commencing at a point on the International Boundary due south of the western extremity of the Cypress Hills, thence west along the said boundary to the central range of the Rocky Mountains, or to the boundary of the Province of British Columbia, thence north-westerly along the said boundary to a point due west of the source of the main branch of the Red Deer River, thence south-westerly and southerly following on the boundaries of the Tracts ceded by the Treaties numbered six and four to the place of commencement

blurb.en: Alberta is named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, a daughter of Queen Victoria. Lake Louise in the Rocky Mountains is named after her too.
blurb.fr: L'Alberta porte le nom de la princesse Louise Caroline Alberta, une fille de la reine Victoria. Le lac Louise, dans les Rocheuses, porte aussi son nom.

source.quote: The province, and the world-famous Lake Louise in the Rocky Mountains, were both named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, fourth daughter of Queen Victoria.

verification.evidence: The province, and the world-famous Lake Louise in the Rocky Mountains, were both named after Princess Louise Caroline Alberta, fourth daughter of Queen Victoria.

blurb.en: Ranching is part of agriculture, one of Canada's natural resource industries. Forestry, fishing, agriculture, mining and energy helped build the country, and many parts of Canada still depend on them.
blurb.fr: L'élevage fait partie de l'agriculture, l'une des industries des ressources naturelles du Canada. La foresterie, la pêche, l'agriculture, les mines et l'énergie ont aidé à bâtir le pays, et de nombreuses régions du Canada en dépendent encore.

source.quote: Natural resources industries include forestry, fishing, agriculture, mining and energy. These industries have played an important part in the country's history and development.

verification.evidence: Natural resources industries include forestry, fishing, agriculture, mining and energy. These industries have played an important part in the country’s history and development. Today, the economy of many areas of the country still depends on developing natural resources

blurb.en: Alberta produces more oil and gas than anywhere else in Canada.
blurb.fr: L'Alberta produit plus de pétrole et de gaz que partout ailleurs au Canada.

source.quote: Alberta is the largest producer of oil and gas

verification.evidence: Alberta is the largest producer of oil and gas, and the oil sands in the north are being developed as a major energy source.

blurb.en: Alberta is famous for farming, and most of all for its huge cattle ranches. Those herds put Canada among the world's biggest beef producers.
blurb.fr: L'Alberta est réputée pour l'agriculture, et surtout pour ses immenses ranchs de bovins. Ces troupeaux placent le Canada parmi les plus grands producteurs de bœuf au monde.

source.quote: Alberta is also renowned for agriculture, especially for the vast cattle ranches that make Canada one of the world's major beef producers.

verification.evidence: Alberta is also renowned for agriculture, especially for the vast cattle ranches that make Canada one of the world’s major beef producers.
